subject: Human Body
title: Baby Bones
description: A short lesson to help you apply Baby Bones.

hook.text: A baby is born with about 270 bones. An adult has 206. Where do the extras go? They fuse together.

buildup.text: Many infant bones are partly cartilage. This flexibility helps during birth and allows rapid growth.

discovery.text: Skull bones fuse at sutures. Hip bones start as three pieces and merge into one by your mid-twenties.

twist.text: A baby's skeleton is so flexible that fractures from simple falls are rare. Soft bones absorb impact.

climax.text: By age 25, fusion is complete and your final bone count locks in at 206. The number never changes again.

punchline.text: Born with 270 bones. End with 206. Fusion is growing up.

quiz.question: Why do babies have more bones than adults?
options: Extra bones break down with age
Many bones fuse together during growth
Adults absorb calcium from excess bones
